Malaria (caused by *Plasmodium*) and cholera (caused by *Vibrio cholerae*) are infectious diseases caused by germs, not by genes, so P and Q are wrong. R (haemophilia and colour blindness) and S (haemophilia and albinism) both list only genetic disorders.

During **ventricular systole** the ventricles contract and the pressure inside them rises. This pushes the **atrioventricular (tricuspid and bicuspid) valves** shut, which stops blood from flowing back into the atria (this produces the first heart sound, 'lubb'). The same pressure pushes the **semilunar valves** open, so blood is forced into the pulmonary artery and the aorta.

So the answer is option (A), P close and Q open.

- A + T = \(300 - (75 + 75) = 150\)
- Since A = T, T = \(150 \div 2 = 75\)

answers.working:
Colour blindness is a **sex-linked recessive** disorder carried on the X chromosome. A son always gets his Y chromosome from his father and his X chromosome from his mother.

Cross: mother \(\mathrm{X^C X}\) (carrier) \(\times\) father \(\mathrm{XY}\) (normal)

| | \(\mathrm{X^C}\) | \(\mathrm{X}\) |
|---|---|---|
| \(\mathrm{X}\) | \(\mathrm{X^C X}\) carrier daughter | \(\mathrm{XX}\) normal daughter |
| \(\mathrm{Y}\) | \(\mathrm{X^C Y}\) colour blind son | \(\mathrm{XY}\) normal son |

Of the two possible sons, one (\(\mathrm{X^C Y}\)) is colour blind and one (\(\mathrm{XY}\)) is normal, so each son has a 50% chance of being colour blind. (Out of all the children, only 25% would be colour blind sons, but the question asks about the sons.)

So the answer is option (B), 50%.

answers.working:
The **sympathetic nervous system** prepares the body for emergencies ('fight or flight'). When Bharat panics about missing the bus, it widens the air passages (**bronchodilation**) so that more air reaches the lungs, and it also raises the heartbeat and breathing rate.

The other options are effects of the parasympathetic system or the opposite of what happens: the coronary arteries dilate (not constrict) and the breathing rate increases (not decreases).

So the answer is option (D), bronchodilation.

answers.value: Right Atrium, Right Ventricle, Lungs, Left Atrium, Left Ventricle, Body tissues
answers.working:
Deoxygenated blood from the body enters the **right atrium**, passes into the **right ventricle**, and is pumped through the pulmonary artery to the **lungs** (pulmonary circulation). Oxygenated blood returns through the pulmonary veins to the **left atrium**, passes into the **left ventricle**, and is pumped through the aorta to the **body tissues** (systemic circulation).

Blood always moves from an atrium to the ventricle below it, never from a ventricle back to an atrium, which rules out options (B) and (C).

So the answer is option (A).

answers.value: Medulla oblongata
answers.working:
Constriction of the pupil in bright light is a **reflex action** controlled by the brain, not by any part of the eye itself. A head injury that stops this reflex points to damage in the brain, and of the options given only the **medulla oblongata** is a part of the brain; it controls many involuntary actions.

The suspensory ligaments and the eye lens are concerned with focusing (accommodation), and the eyelid only covers the eye, so none of them controls the size of the pupil.

So the answer is option (B), medulla oblongata.

Note: strictly, the centre of the pupil reflex lies in the midbrain, which is not an option; the medulla oblongata is the only brain structure offered.
answers.flag: Strictly the pupillary light reflex centre is in the midbrain, not the medulla oblongata. Medulla is the only brain option and clearly the intended answer; a note says so to the student.

**Albuminuria** is the presence of protein (albumin) in the urine. It happens when the glomeruli of the kidney are damaged and let large protein molecules filter through.

Haematuria is blood in the urine, glycosuria is glucose in the urine, and anaemia is a shortage of haemoglobin or RBCs in the blood.

So the answer is option (C), albuminuria.

If the ovum is not fertilised, the corpus luteum degenerates and the level of progesterone falls. The thickened lining of the uterus (**endometrium**) then breaks down and is shed along with blood. This flow is called menstruation, and it occurs in the **menstrual phase** (about days 1 to 5 of the cycle).

So the answer is option (C), menstrual phase.

**(b)** Odd one: **Vasopressin**. The others (growth hormone, thyroid stimulating hormone, gonadotropic hormone) are **hormones of the anterior pituitary**; vasopressin (ADH) is released by the posterior pituitary.

|---|---|

answers.value: Interphase
answers.working: **Interphase** is the resting stage of the cell cycle. The cell is not dividing, but it is metabolically very active: it grows, makes proteins and replicates (doubles) its DNA in preparation for the next division.

answers.value: Depth perception: judging distance accurately
answers.working:
In **binocular vision** both eyes face forward and see the same object at the same time, but from slightly different angles. The brain combines the two images into one three-dimensional image.

The advantage is **perception of depth**: the eagle can judge the distance of its prey accurately, which lets it swoop down and catch the prey precisely while flying at high speed.

answers.value: Labelled diagram of animal cell in prophase with four chromosomes
answers.working:
Draw a round animal cell (no cell wall) bounded by a **cell membrane**, with the following features:

- **Nucleus** in the centre whose **nuclear membrane** is drawn as a broken (dotted) line, because it is beginning to disappear in prophase. The **nucleolus** is drawn small and faint, as it is also disappearing.
- **Four chromosomes** inside the nucleus, drawn short and thick (the chromatin has condensed). Each chromosome is made of two **sister chromatids** joined at a **centromere**. Show them as two long and two short chromosomes, scattered and not yet in a line.
- Two pairs of **centrioles**, one pair moving towards each opposite pole of the cell, each surrounded by star-like rays (**asters**).
- The first **spindle fibres** beginning to form between the two centriole pairs.
- **Cytoplasm** around the nucleus.

Labels to give: cell membrane, cytoplasm, nuclear membrane (disintegrating), nucleolus (disappearing), chromosome, chromatid, centromere, centriole, aster, spindle fibres. Give the diagram the title 'Prophase in an animal cell'.
